meta.subject: science
meta.title: Acids, Bases, Salts & Chemical Reactions
meta.titleLocal: अम्ल, क्षार, लवण र रासायनिक प्रतिक्रिया
meta.summary: Indicators and pH, neutralisation and salts, reaction signs and gas tests, and balancing equations, in four virtual lab stations.

chunks.title: Sour, bitter, slippery
body: Lemons and vinegar taste **sour**: they contain **acids**.
Soap feels **slippery** and baking soda tastes **bitter**: they are **bases**.
We never taste lab chemicals! Instead we use **indicators**: dyes that change colour.

chunks.title: Station 1 · Dropper & Colour Detective
intro: Pick an indicator, then click a tube to test it.
Fill in the detective's notebook, then try **Mystery mode**!

challenges.text: **Mission:** in Mystery mode, find a tube that turns phenolphthalein **pink** and red litmus **blue**.
challenges.explain: Only a base turns phenolphthalein pink and red litmus blue.

challenges.text: Test all **six** tubes with at least one indicator.

question.prompt: A solution turns **phenolphthalein pink**. What kind of solution is it?

options.why: Neutral solutions like pure water keep it colourless too.
You can! Phenolphthalein turns pink **only** in a base.

question.explanation: Phenolphthalein: colourless in acids and neutral solutions, **pink in bases**.

chunks.title: Zoom in: the pH scale
chunks.intro: Tap the **ACID** or **BASE** bottle to drip, or pick a liquid. Acids crowd with $\text{H}^+$; bases with $\text{OH}^-$.

challenges.text: Find the pH where $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{OH}^-$ balance out.
challenges.explain: At pH 7, H⁺ and OH⁻ balance out: neutral, like pure water.

chunks.title: Neutralisation
body: Add a base to an acid and they cancel each other out. This is **neutralisation**.
It gives out heat, so it is **exothermic**.

chunks.title: Station 2 · The Salt Factory
intro: The beaker holds acid with **universal indicator** (red, pH 1).
Tap the burette tap or the drop buttons. Aim for **green, pH 7**!

challenges.text: **Mission:** neutralise the $\text{HCl}$ beaker with $\text{NaOH}$ to exactly pH 7 and crystallise common table salt, $\text{NaCl}$!
challenges.explain: The acid and base cancelled out, leaving water and table salt, $\text{NaCl}$.

challenges.text: Overshoot to purple, rescue it with acid drops, then crystallise.

chunks.title: Salt name = metal + acid ending
body: The **first** word comes from the metal in the base (sodium, potassium, magnesium).
The **second** comes from the acid (chloride, sulphate, nitrate).

chunks.title: Mini-game · Real-life cures
chunks.intro: Neutralisation fixes everyday problems. Pick the right remedy for each one.

challenges.explain: Each problem was an acid, so a mild base neutralised it.

question.prompt: Hydrochloric acid + potassium hydroxide → potassium ___ + water

mistakes.why: The hydroxide comes from the base, and it turns into **water**. The salt's second word comes from the acid.
That ending belongs to a different acid. **Hydro-chlor-ic** acid makes **chlor-ide** salts.

chunks.title: Is it a chemical reaction?
body: - A precipitate (a solid that appears in a liquid)

chunks.title: Station 3 · Bubble, Pop & Precipitate
chunks.intro: Tap the jars and the matchstick. Spot every sign of a chemical change!

challenges.text: **Mission:** make hydrogen gas and prove it with the **pop test**.
challenges.explain: Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop. That's the test for $\text{H}_2$!

challenges.text: **Mission:** produce a gas that turns clear lime water **milky**!
Fast-forward the iron nail a full **20 minutes**.
Spot all **4 signs** of a chemical reaction.

options.why: Hydrogen's test is the squeaky **pop** with a burning match. It doesn't change lime water.
Oxygen's test is relighting a **glowing** splint.
Nitrogen does nothing to lime water.

question.explanation: $\text{CO}_2$ reacts with lime water to make white, insoluble calcium carbonate: $\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3\downarrow + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

chunks.title: Atoms are never lost
body: In a reaction, atoms are only **rearranged**. None are made or destroyed.
So the total mass stays the same: the **law of conservation of mass**.
A **balanced equation** has the same number of each kind of atom on both sides.

chunks.title: Station 4 · The Seesaw Equation Builder
intro: Reactant atoms sit on the left, product atoms on the right.
Change the big numbers in front of each formula until the seesaw levels out.

challenges.explain: $2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$: 4 H and 2 O atoms on each side.

options.why: Those are the **reactants**: they're on the left, before the arrow.
Zinc is a reactant (left of the arrow). Products are everything on the right.
HCl is a reactant. Products are made **by** the reaction, after the arrow.

question.explanation: Reactants → products. The arrow means "turns into".

flashcards.back:
Tastes sour, pH below 7, turns blue litmus **red**.
Lemon juice, vinegar, $\text{HCl}$

Tastes bitter, feels soapy, pH above 7, turns red litmus **blue**.
Soap, baking soda, $\text{NaOH}$

Colourless in acid and neutral.
**Pink** in base.

**Red** in acid.
Yellow in neutral and base.

Yellow in acid and neutral.
**Reddish-brown** in base.
Bubble it through lime water → turns **milky**.

Atoms are rearranged, never created or destroyed.
Balanced equation: same atoms on both sides.

questions.prompt: You add phenolphthalein to a clear solution and it **stays colourless**. What can you say?

options.why: Careful! Phenolphthalein is also colourless in **neutral** solutions like pure water. Use litmus to tell them apart.
It could be water, but an acid also keeps phenolphthalein colourless.

hints: Which kinds of solution turn phenolphthalein pink?
Only bases turn it pink. So if it stays colourless, it isn't a base.
Not a base → it's an **acid or neutral**. Phenolphthalein alone can't tell which.
questions.explanation: Colourless phenolphthalein rules out a base, but can't separate acid from neutral.

questions.prompt: A few drops of **methyl orange** are added to soap water (a base). What colour do you see?

options.why: Methyl orange turns **red in acids**. Soap water is a base.
Pink in a base is **phenolphthalein**, not methyl orange.
Green in a base is the **China rose** indicator.

hints: Is soap water an acid or a base?
Methyl orange is red in acid and changes colour above about pH 4.
In a base methyl orange is **yellow**.
questions.explanation: Methyl orange: red in acid, yellow in neutral and basic solutions.

questions.prompt: Sulphuric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium ___ + water

mistakes.why: Close! But sulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) contains oxygen, so its salts are **sulphates**.

hints: The second word of a salt's name comes from the acid.
Sulphuric acid has $\text{SO}_4$ in it. That group is called sulph-___.
questions.explanation: Sulphuric acid makes **sulphate** salts: sodium sulphate, $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$.

questions.prompt: Nitric acid + potassium hydroxide → potassium ___ + water

mistakes.why: Nitric acid ($\text{HNO}_3$) contains oxygen, so its salts end in **-ate**.
Chloride comes from hydrochloric acid, not nitric acid.
The hydroxide turns into water. The salt's second word comes from the acid.

hints: Which part of the name comes from the acid?
questions.explanation: Nitric acid makes **nitrate** salts: potassium nitrate, $\text{KNO}_3$.

options.why: Those are the **products**: they're made by the reaction, after the arrow.
Hydrogen is a product (right of the arrow).
Magnesium is a reactant too: everything on the left of the arrow reacts.

hints: Reactants are what you start with: everything **before** the arrow.

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are on the **left** side of $2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$? ___

mistakes.why: The big 2 in front means **two** $\text{H}_2$ molecules, each with 2 H atoms: $2 \times 2$.
Only count hydrogen, and only on the left: $2\text{H}_2$ gives $2 \times 2$ H atoms.

hints: The big number in front multiplies the whole molecule.
$\text{H}_2$ has 2 H atoms, and there are 2 of them.
$2 \times 2 = 4$ hydrogen atoms (and 4 on the right too: it's balanced).

items.title: Naming salts
items.body: Metal from the base + ending from the acid: potassium nitrate.

items.title: Gas tests
items.body: Balanced equation: same number of each atom on both sides.
